content.content: {"result":"{\"documentId\": \"f_6feda53b2382c63bf47b25\", \"title\": \"Angel note: how to count the money\", \"name\": \"Angel note: how to count the money\", \"revisionId\": \"a7f6f837df\", \"createdTime\": \"2026-02-12T23:52:18Z\", \"modifiedTime\": \"2026-02-13T00:41:06Z\", \"text\": \"Angel note: how to count the money\\nAngels will ask what each bet cost and what it brought in. This is how we count it so the three of us say the same thing. It replaces the quick plan I left on our board.\\nGo by the bank. SVB\\u2019s Payment Processed notices are the one place I know with a line per payment, and what the banks say is our ground source of truth. Start at the first SVB wires in Sep 2023 and stop at the last run on Feb 2. Anything paid out of Chase isn\\u2019t in here.\\nWhat counts is money that left the company and stayed out. A notice is where you start, not the last word. Take a notice as paid unless one of us has said the money came back. If someone we paid closes out their file with us and tells us what they received, that beats the notices for them. Money we moved between our own accounts isn\\u2019t spending, no bucket for that. Every payee keeps its line, even at zero.\\nIf we paid a contractor some other way, it goes in only if a receipt for it reached your mail, at the amount sent, not the fee.\\nBuckets. Build is the team on Deel plus the studios and freelancers who made the games. Everything on Deel counts as team, don\\u2019t try to split it. Marketing is anything made or bought to get installs (ad networks, agencies, ad creative, playables, trailers): list it under its bet by date like the rest, but keep it out of build cost, I have those numbers. Company is legal, tools, the website, equipment and anything else that wasn\\u2019t for one of the three games: that goes in the Company column. Our own pay and anyone on Gusto aren\\u2019t in here.\\nWhich bet. Go by the Transaction Date on the notice, the whole payment to one bet: Domino Delights up to Jan 8, 2025, ZM from Jan 9, 2025 to Nov 23, 2025, Combo Fighter from Nov 24, 2025. Don\\u2019t try to work out who was on what, that\\u2019s where we\\u2019d start arguing.\\nAnything not paid in dollars stays in its own currency next to the line. Don\\u2019t add it to a dollar total.\\nWhat each game brought in is its lifetime revenue from the warehouse\\u2019s daily revenue table, as recorded. Leave Combo Fighter\\u2019s revenue off for now, on the page, on the deck and when you tell me, until we\\u2019ve checked its first sales.\\nOn the Linear project: move each payee\\u2019s issue to Done once its line is right. If your figure isn\\u2019t what the notices add up to, say why on the issue first.\\n\"}"}

{"documentId": "f_6feda53b2382c63bf47b25", "title": "Angel note: how to count the money", "name": "Angel note: how to count the money", "revisionId": "a7f6f837df", "createdTime": "2026-02-12T23:52:18Z", "modifiedTime": "2026-02-13T00:41:06Z", "text": "Angel note: how to count the money
Angels will ask what each bet cost and what it brought in. This is how we count it so the three of us say the same thing. It replaces the quick plan I left on our board.
Go by the bank. SVB’s Payment Processed notices are the one place I know with a line per payment, and what the banks say is our ground source of truth. Start at the first SVB wires in Sep 2023 and stop at the last run on Feb 2. Anything paid out of Chase isn’t in here.
What counts is money that left the company and stayed out. A notice is where you start, not the last word. Take a notice as paid unless one of us has said the money came back. If someone we paid closes out their file with us and tells us what they received, that beats the notices for them. Money we moved between our own accounts isn’t spending, no bucket for that. Every payee keeps its line, even at zero.
If we paid a contractor some other way, it goes in only if a receipt for it reached your mail, at the amount sent, not the fee.
Buckets. Build is the team on Deel plus the studios and freelancers who made the games. Everything on Deel counts as team, don’t try to split it. Marketing is anything made or bought to get installs (ad networks, agencies, ad creative, playables, trailers): list it under its bet by date like the rest, but keep it out of build cost, I have those numbers. Company is legal, tools, the website, equipment and anything else that wasn’t for one of the three games: that goes in the Company column. Our own pay and anyone on Gusto aren’t in here.
Which bet. Go by the Transaction Date on the notice, the whole payment to one bet: Domino Delights up to Jan 8, 2025, ZM from Jan 9, 2025 to Nov 23, 2025, Combo Fighter from Nov 24, 2025. Don’t try to work out who was on what, that’s where we’d start arguing.
Anything not paid in dollars stays in its own currency next to the line. Don’t add it to a dollar total.
What each game brought in is its lifetime revenue from the warehouse’s daily revenue table, as recorded. Leave Combo Fighter’s revenue off for now, on the page, on the deck and when you tell me, until we’ve checked its first sales.
On the Linear project: move each payee’s issue to Done once its line is right. If your figure isn’t what the notices add up to, say why on the issue first.
"}

Combo Fighter Data and Harmony Games Shut-Down leonard hayes <leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co> Mon, 9 Feb 2026 11:12:35 -0800 ['INBOX', 'Label_b19fb8d1b3', 'CATEGORY_PERSONAL']
Hi PERSON_4337_NAME,

After reviewing the latest Combo Fighter data (see the attached screenshot
from today below) and considering the iterations we’ve already run, we’ve
decided to shut the company down. We don't believe we are VC-investable in
our current form, so continuing to operate while we search for a fundable
direction is not responsible.

I want to align with you on an orderly wind-down and the necessary board
actions. High level topics for the call:

   -

   Proposed board resolution and the plan of dissolution
   -

   Timeline and sequencing (employees, vendors, product shutdown, and
   investor communications)
   -

   Cash and liabilities snapshot, plus what reserves we should hold for
   taxes, payroll, and chargebacks
   -

   Any stockholder approvals or creditor notice steps we should consider
   -

   What, if anything, we should do with the remaining IP and codebase

Can we do a quick call in a day or two? I can send a few time options if
helpful.

Thanks,
Leonard

Retention Data for Combo Fighter as of Feb 9, 2026, makes Harmony Games
non-VC friendly.

• What lovable can do:
    ◦ Build a `/login` page with a *“Continue with Google”* button.
    ◦ Initialize Firebase (copy/paste your `apiKey`, `authDomain`).

    ◦ Paste your Firebase config into lovable.

Option B — Google Identity Services (pure Google OAuth)
• What lovable can do:
    ◦ Render the Google Sign-In button / One Tap.
    ◦ Use the *GIS Token Client* for `openid email profile` and receive an *ID token*.
    ◦ Pass that ID token to your backend.
• What you must do:
    ◦ Create a Google Cloud *OAuth Client ID (Web)*.
    ◦ Add *Authorized JavaScript origins* (e.g., `<http://localhost:5173>`, `<https://engine.Harmony Games>`) and *Redirect URIs* (if using redirect flow).
    ◦ Backend endpoint to *verify the ID token* (use Google libraries), create a *signed session cookie* (httpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax), and return it.
    ◦ (Optional) Enforce Workspace domain by checking the token’s `hd` claim or email domain.

• `POST /auth/session` — accepts an *ID token*, verifies it, issues an *httpOnly session cookie*.

• `POST /auth/logout` — clears the cookie.

import json,re
r=json.load(open('msgs.json'))
have={k.split('/<')[1].rstrip('>') for k in r}
ids=[l.strip() for l in open('ids.txt') if l.strip()]
print('missing',[i for i in ids if i not in have])
out=[]
for k,v in r.items():
  b=re.sub(r'\s+',' ',v['body'])
  if 'svb' not in (v['frm'] or '').lower() and 'SVC_4249' not in (v['frm'] or ''):
    print('NONSVB',v['date'],v['frm'],v['subj']); print(b[:1500]); print(); continue
  def g(p):
    m=re.search(p,b); return m.group(1).strip() if m else ''
  out.append(dict(id=k,date=v['date'],subj=v['subj'],frm_acct=g(r'From: (.*?)To:'),to=g(r'To: (.*?)Amount:'),amt=g(r'Amount: (.*?)Transaction Date:'),txn=g(r'Transaction Date: (\w+ \d+ \d{4})'),extra=g(r'Delivery Date: (.*?)Payment Reference')))
json.dump(out,open('svb.json','w'),indent=0)
print(len(out))
EOF

import json,datetime,collections
s=json.load(open('svb.json'))
def d(x): return datetime.datetime.strptime(x,'%b %d %Y').date()
def bet(dt):
  if dt<=datetime.date(2025,1,8): return 'DD'
  if dt<=datetime.date(2025,11,23): return 'ZM'
  return 'CF'
def key(to):
  t=to
  if '8380' in t: return 'Deel'
  if '4015' in t: return 'Singular'
  if 'BANCO' in t: return 'MotMot'
  return t
agg=collections.defaultdict(lambda: collections.defaultdict(float))
cnt=collections.Counter()
for r in s:
  dt=d(r['txn']); amt,cur=r['amt'].rsplit(' ',1); amt=float(amt.replace(',',''))

<@EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID> the angel page is done. It's set up like your working sheet, sits in my Drive, and you and Blake both have edit access: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SCFJAYHmM35L3SxP76TJkoc3TBvkAqPpaiF0xd5qZio/edit

**What each bet cost to build** (Deel + studios + freelancers, counted your way):
• Domino Delights: **$951,817.64** (~$952K)
• ZM: **$544,433.44** (~$544K)
• Combo Fighter: **$72,685.61** (~$73K)

**What each brought in** (lifetime revenue, warehouse daily revenue table as recorded):
• Domino Delights: **$12,331.25** (~$12.3K)
• ZM: **$11.99**
• Combo Fighter: left off, as you asked

**What changes on the draft deck**
• Build slide: DD $985K → **$952K**, ZM $609K → **$544K**, CF $74K → **$73K**
• "What each brought in": replace "to fill in" with **DD $12.3K, ZM $12**, and leave CF off

**Why your quick numbers came down:** your quick pass took every USD notice by date, and those totals tie exactly to the 132 notices. The gap is what your doc takes out:
• Marketing pulled out of build: DD $16.4K (Node Media), ZM $56.5K (Adjoe, AppLovin, PlayableX, Telegram UA), CF $1K. It's still listed under each bet on the page.
• Company items moved to the Company column: $49,625 (TYZ, trademarks, JP's website, Singular, 4X proposal). Martin's laptop was paid in lev, so it sits there as 1,999.00 BGN and isn't in any dollar total.
• DD changes:
  ◦ Leapblock's close-out adds $33,290, a Sep 13, 2023 wire that has no SVB notice. Their statement wins.
  ◦ The $4,032 MotMot wire that came back is out.
  ◦ The $4,000 to JPMorgan was our own Chase account, so it's a zero line.
  ◦ Oleg's $125 came back and there's no Payoneer receipt in my mail, so that's zero too.

All 22 Payee history issues are now Done. Before closing them I left a comment on each one whose figure isn't what the notices add up to: Leapblock, MotMot, JPMorgan and Oleg.

I built the page as a sheet in your Drive, laid out like Leonard's working sheet, and gave him and Blake edit access. All 22 Payee history issues are Done, and I replied to him in #winddown with the numbers and the deck changes ([message](https://harmonygamesgroup.slack.com/archives/C0ADGSZKR3R/p1771027855000000)).

**Sheet:** https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1SCFJAYHmM35L3SxP76TJkoc3TBvkAqPpaiF0xd5qZio/edit

| Bet | Cost to build | Brought in | Draft deck now says |
|---|---|---|---|
| Domino Delights | $951,817.64 (~$952K) | $12,331.25 (~$12.3K) | $985K |
| ZM | $544,433.44 (~$544K) | $11.99 | $609K |
| Combo Fighter | $72,685.61 (~$73K) | left off, as Leonard asked | $74K |

"Brought in" is lifetime revenue from the warehouse's daily revenue table, as recorded.

**Deck changes I gave Leonard:**
- **Build cost slide:** change to $952K, $544K and $73K.
- **"What each brought in" slide:** fill in DD $12.3K and ZM $12, and leave Combo Fighter off.

His quick numbers are all the SVB "Payment Processed" notices added up by date, and they match the 132 notices to the cent. Ours come out lower for these reasons:
- **Marketing taken out of build cost:** $16.4K for Domino Delights, $56.5K for ZM and $1K for Combo Fighter. It's still listed under each bet on the page.
- **Company items moved to the Company column ($49,625):** the law firm, trademark filings, the website, Singular and the 4X proposal. Martin's laptop was paid in Bulgarian lev, so it sits there as 1,999.00 BGN and isn't in any dollar total.
- **Four lines differ from the notices.** Each has a comment on its Linear issue explaining why, posted before I closed it:
  - **Leapblock: +$33,290.** Their accountant's close-out in the #leapblock channel lists a Sep 13, 2023 wire that has no SVB notice. Per Leonard's rules, a payee's own close-out beats the notices.
  - **MotMot: −$4,032.** One April 2024 wire went to a wrong account and came back, so it's counted once.
  - **JPMorgan: $4,000 → $0.** Blake confirmed by email that it went to our own Chase account.
  - **Oleg: $125 → $0.** The wire came back the same day. Leonard re-sent it through Payoneer, but there's no Payoneer receipt in your mail, so it doesn't count.

Two of the bucket calls were mine, so check that you agree:
- **Singular:** I put it under Company because Leonard's Linear note calls it "attribution tool, not one game." One could argue it's marketing; it doesn't change build cost either way.
- **The unnamed LLC paid $16,428.57 on Jan 2, 2025:** emails show it's Node Media, a UA agency, so I put it under Marketing for Domino Delights.
